fields.title: Managed processor invocations with portable isolation and durable recovery
fields.description:
## Outcome
An application can execute registered native workloads on untrusted inputs through one Runledger-owned invocation path without implementing launch, timeout, cancellation, join, cleanup or retry coordination. Feasibility evidence selects the execution approach; a local-plus-custom-remote adapter pair is not predetermined. The same protected application contract must work in two materially different deployment models under explicit, verified prerequisites. No provider-specific topology is imposed on the application API.

## Scope and authority
This epic is the canonical cross-task decision record. Child Beads own delivery scope, acceptance, priority, status and native blocker edges. Stable T-01 through T-08 identifiers are retained in task titles and external references; there is no parallel Markdown backlog.

The requested work is planning. Implementation tasks remain open and unclaimed. Implementation includes native Runledger contracts/persistence/runtime, only the execution bindings required by the selected deployment models, a generic consumer and conformance evidence. The draft-PR workflow is authorized. Infrastructure provisioning, hosted deployment and publication require their own authorization; this planning epic does not authorize them. Do not modify the motivating application's active migration as part of this epic.

Ordinary handlers keep their existing supported contracts. The new protected processor path must not silently select a weaker backend. Unix-only scope remains; Linux and macOS controllers stay in scope, with unsupported local isolation capabilities explicitly rejected and remote execution available where verified.

## Evidence
Fact: source inspected at 74238a2dffe29aee681440c566d6bcb42e742e30. runledger/runledger-core/src/jobs/{handler,execution,status}.rs provide trusted handlers, live deadlines/progress and retry kinds. runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs stops polling a handler after deadline or lease loss; it does not establish external-process termination.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Durable execution resources, and runledger/migrations/202607280004_job_execution_resources.up.sql define lease-scoped single-permit reservations released through job transitions/reaping. These cannot bound executions that survive their job lease.
Fact: native settlement lives in runledger/runledger-runtime/src/{settlement,task_group,supervisor}/. runledger/runledger-postgres/src/jobs/queue/{claim,reaper,lifecycle}.rs and associated directories own queue transitions; reuse them rather than adding a second queue.
Fact: an inspected upload-processing consumer's repair history repeatedly addressed disposable-container cleanup, parser/host failure attribution and bounded retries. Its unfinished migration replaced container launch with environment-cleared subprocesses. Source inspection is not executed isolation evidence; no defect-rate or final-consumer claim is made. This anonymized rationale is sufficient; another private checkout is not an implementation prerequisite.
Fact: crates/batter-sqlx/src/atomic/scope.rs exposes PgScopedSql::executor and explicitly permits SQL with irreversible effects such as COMMIT; boundary-loss detection is not rollback. The inspected regression source crates/batter-sqlx/tests/atomic_live/fail_fast_loss.rs exercises committed writes despite scope loss. runledger-postgres/src/atomic.rs reuses that capability, while jobs/queue/lifecycle/success.rs currently owns its own transaction. These sources were inspected, not executed, during this amendment.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Quick start, supports separate producer and worker processes sharing PostgreSQL. Hosting an existing trusted worker beside a proven local executor is a candidate deployment, not proof of processor isolation.
Inference: reusable execution ownership and isolation-binding contracts can remove this repeated application protocol, but backend support, operator burden and deployment assumptions must be demonstrated.
Existing related work: batter-44w, batter-gg8 and batter-0cp are completed foundations, not proof of this capability. batter-7g0 concerns diagnostic correlation and must not become an authority prerequisite.

## Verification and completion
All eight delivery tasks must meet their acceptance. The same representative registered native workload and hostile fixture corpus must execute through the two selected deployment models. A fake adapter, loopback transport or a second identical host alone is insufficient isolation or deployment-diversity evidence. Cover controller/runner death, delayed launch after cancellation, lease takeover, result/commit uncertainty, descendant escape attempts, resource/output exhaustion, credential/filesystem/network denial, current-authority rejection and upgrade/retention compatibility. Include fresh-agent implementation and modification exercises; label them proposed/unexecuted until recorded.

Use focused checks during each task and the repository's applicable complete backend verification before delivery. Record exact revisions, operating systems, backend versions, commands, prerequisites and results in the owning Bead. Update rustdoc/examples, relevant contracts, implemented-status rows, docs/references.md and verification input ownership when implementation lands. Do not present this planning session as runtime, Linux/macOS or hosted-CI verification.

## Rollout and recovery
Use additive migrations and versioned invocation/protocol/profile identifiers. Keep processor dispatch disabled until database guards and every active worker/reaper/admin writer that could claim, reap, replay, cancel or purge processor jobs are compatible or fenced out. Job-type filtering alone does not protect old reapers. Prefer a coordinated cutover when it meets deployment needs; mixed-version operation is not a goal by itself. Preserve legacy job semantics and test actual old/new binaries, including an old session/transaction resumed across activation, against the selected writer-exclusion policy.
Start with synthetic inputs. Stop new processor admission on containment; durably record stop intent, revoke further input access, reconcile outstanding invocations and retain their capacity/tombstones. Plaintext already delivered cannot be recalled. A failed job or expired lease does not prove stopped execution. Never clear an unresolved execution as a normal retry or delete applied schema/history for rollback. Disabling admission must leave a compatible recovery owner running.
Normal bounded shutdown may hand remote recovery to a durable owner only after acknowledged persistence and settlement of local users of dependencies. Report that handoff separately from remote termination; it is not a clean external-execution result.

## Risks and open decisions
T-01 owns the first protected profile, representative processor, deployment selection, failure assumptions, physical execution multiplicity, result-handoff strategy and operational cost. Compare separate native workers with local isolation, an existing managed executor, and a narrow remote runner on equal footing. Limit the comparison to those three topology families and actual mechanism proofs to at most two shortlisted choices; use one representative registered native workload plus hostile fixtures. A new remote service is justified only by a demonstrated trust/deployment need.
T-01 closure must record the chosen models, exact privileges/services/inventories and operating owner, an actionable uncertainty-recovery exercise, and the deployment tests required to establish the intended supported environments. It must revise D-07 and T-05/T-06 scope/edges to its findings before T-02 closes. It can choose a simpler topology without weakening the protected contract or removing deployment-diversity evidence. If no candidate meets the selected required profile, retain the blocker; do not invent a sandbox or silently weaken a guarantee.
T-02 closes only after the SQL capability boundary, result-copy ownership/acknowledgements, backend retry/multiplicity rules and a small compiling consumer are explicit. T-03 owns locking, reservations and writer activation. T-08 rehearses an already designed recovery procedure and records final deployment evidence. Application authorization, application-level result correctness, application content policy, external publication and forensic erasure remain outside library guarantees.
Strict no-overlap and workflow-lineage coverage remain the initial supported policy, with their availability cost recorded in D-05; they are not logical consequences of handling untrusted inputs. Accounted overlapping transformations or a direct-jobs-only scope are alternatives requiring an explicit contract/scope amendment, not implementation shortcuts.
The first safe delivery action is T-01; later implementation is conditional on its closure decisions. After T-02, persistence and the first execution binding can proceed independently when shared interfaces settle. Runtime follows persistence. The second deployment task depends on the first binding only if selected reuse requires it; record that edge before either dependent task starts. fields.design:
## Decisions and design
D-01 — Accepted planning direction: general managed processor invocations.
The contract owns execution of registered native workloads with bounded opaque inputs and results. Payload schemas, domain interpretation, intake/storage workflows and business authorization belong to downstream applications. Feasibility fixtures exercise execution requirements and do not define library-specific content types or domain processors.
The application supplies an authorized bounded input and interprets the result. Runledger owns registration, durable admission/identity, execution, deadline enforcement, result fencing, settlement and recovery. An adapter owns concrete execution/transport; deployment owns provisioning and enforcing external identity/network/storage configuration. Processors receive no database, key-store or orchestration authority. A trusted broker or native worker is distinct from the untrusted payload processor. A separate Runledger-specific remote service is optional.

D-02 — Accepted: one concrete, fail-closed initial profile; defer a general profile language.
T-01 must define the initial profile before evaluating mechanisms. Assume a fully compromised registered native executable. Name protected secrets, other inputs, broker/worker authority and host resources; allowed channels/files/egress; input/output, CPU, memory, process-count, scratch and duration bounds; and the exact controller/broker/host failure assumptions. Select only the confidentiality/disposal properties required for this first profile. Bind a registered processor/revision to that validated contract, with fresh per-invocation containment; reuse of compromised native processor state is deferred. Required unsupported or unknown properties reject before sensitive input release. An explicit unresolved outcome preserves failure evidence; it never counts as satisfying a requested hard resource or lifetime bound. Distinguish memory-only from encrypted ephemeral scratch, cooperative cancellation from executor-side lifetime enforcement, and process supervision from isolation. Deployment assumptions and evidence have provenance; a Rust witness is not proof of remote configuration. The application chooses a declared profile; adapters cannot weaken it. Processor executable/entrypoint and permitted options are fixed by trusted registration. Untrusted input/result fields cannot select commands, images, mounts, host paths or arbitrary fetch URLs; artifact descriptors are scoped capabilities, not unchecked path/URL strings.

D-03 — Accepted: library-owned phase order.
A canonical processor-job registration supplies trusted preparation and application callbacks around runtime-owned admission -> durable intent -> authorized input transfer -> execution -> candidate-result handoff -> required execution/scratch settlement -> fenced application and native completion -> candidate-result disposal. Preparation may reject without launching; authorize/audit immediately before plaintext transfer, and revalidate authority after any capacity/startup wait. Avoid holding plaintext while awaiting unbounded admission. Work factories are inert before polling/admission. T-01 selects one initial input/result-transfer approach: bounded native streams or explicitly scoped immutable artifact access. Do not build both without a demonstrated need, or persist raw bytes, reusable grants or presigned URLs as queue metadata.
Keep generic contracts free of storage/provider dependencies. Extend native persistence/runtime; keep mechanism-specific SDKs and tooling optional. The Batter adapter only integrates native startup/shutdown and reexports justified native APIs.

D-04 — Accepted: durable invocation identity and independent evidence.
Persist a stable execution identity linked to job/run/attempt, immutable input identity, processor/profile revision, backend binding, absolute durable expiry and bounded sanitized observations before launch. Never serialize a local Instant. Work budgets cannot grow on restart or through transport delay. Specify a trusted time source and conservative conversion to local monotonic clocks, an explicit tolerated skew bound and fail-closed behavior when expiry cannot be established. Name the trusted component that independently arms/enforces expiry and the allowed enforcement delay for each supported failure domain. Prove controller/broker loss while the processor environment remains alive; killing their shared host/container proves a different property. Cover restart/reboot, suspend/resume and clock rollback within the stated fault model. Settlement has its own bounded observation allowance without extending work authority.
Result receipt, accepted result, stop intent, stopped observation and required cleanup are separate facts. NotStarted, returned, rejected, failed and unresolved conditions need exhaustive handling. Returned output cannot authorize application/native success before required execution/scratch settlement and durable ownership of any retained result. Each reservation releases only on evidence for its own obligation; bounded candidate-result disposal may remain durably pending after application/native completion and must not be reported as complete cleanup. The runtime retains those obligations if the caller drops a waiter, ignores the result or returns success.
Backend start/observe/stop/recover operations have stable identity, bounded idempotency/retention and late-launch semantics. Reject conflicting same-identity requests. Cancellation must survive a delayed start, broker restart and identity reuse attempts. Not-found is conclusive only under the backend's absence/fencing guarantee. Retain uncertainty otherwise. Processor self-reported exit is not independent termination evidence.
A backend request/job identity is not assumed to identify exactly one physical execution. Before persistence design, T-01/T-02 must establish executor-internal retry/restart/replacement ownership, physical execution identities and aggregate admission, input grants and elapsed/resource budgets. The initial strict profile requires at most one active physical processor in its lineage; an executor that can launch an uncontrolled duplicate is unsupported even if its API retry count is zero. A bounded execution-group/overlap contract is a separate future decision, not an implicit reinterpretation of one reserved slot. Test replacement initiated by the substrate without another Runledger dispatch.

D-05 — Accepted: capacity and recovery outlive job leases.
Use native durable reservations associated with invocations, reconciled independently of the current job lease. Uncertain launches and possibly live executions remain accounted across retry, cancellation, dead-lettering, reaping and worker death. Define protected no-overlap over a stable native invocation lineage for one logical processor job/workflow step, preserved by direct replay and workflow recovery even when new job/run IDs are allocated. No replacement execution in that lineage while the previous one remains unresolved. Workflow active-key/resource release must consider outstanding processor invocations, not only live canceled leases. New unrelated roots are not globally deduplicated by content hash; applications use explicit resource/idempotency policy when they require cross-root exclusion. Bound outstanding unknown executions and admission waiters across replicas; do not add a general quota engine. Compute, sensitive scratch and retained candidate-result obligations may settle at different times and require separately bounded accounting. Retention/purge cannot cascade away unresolved records, reservations or late-launch tombstones.
Strict no-overlap is an explicit conservative first-release policy: it avoids introducing an overlapping-replay contract while preserving existing workflow resource/exclusion expectations. It can block a lineage indefinitely under uncertainty; T-01 must establish whether that availability cost and containment procedure are acceptable. Side-effect-free duplicates can be valid under another contract with complete aggregate accounting and fenced acceptance; they are not inherently a security defect, but are not enabled here. Workflow coverage is retained; omitting it requires explicit rejection of unsupported processor workflow compositions and a scope amendment.
Use the existing native recovery machinery. A remote runner may use native invocation persistence or its selected executor's durable inventory, but must not grow a second job queue, workflow engine or fleet manager. Recovery control is trusted; the untrusted processor has only the exact input/result channel. Reserve bounded control/reconciliation resources so saturated execution admission cannot prevent recovery. T-01 rehearses full-capacity loss of observability and identifies the responsible operator, real execution-domain identity, supported containment action and evidence permitting reuse. If that evidence is unavailable, expose quarantined/unavailable capacity; deleting rows or operator approval alone is not settlement evidence.
Retries require explicit replay policy, established prior-execution eligibility and finite attempt/elapsed limits. Adapter observations determine infrastructure failures; processor bytes cannot invent them. Indeterminate and deterministic resource-limit failures cannot open an unlimited alternative retry budget.

D-06 — Accepted: untrusted results and fenced application effects.
Bound and validate transport envelopes and output; bind them to invocation, input and processor/profile revision. Require authenticated encryption with peer/endpoint verification for every remote control, input and result hop; authentication alone is insufficient. Any buffered sensitive artifacts obey the selected confidentiality/retention profile. Authenticate narrowly scoped grants; consider replay, wrong audience, expiry, wrong-attempt results and metadata-service/ambient-credential access. Define the authorization linearization point and any online redemption/revocation check or bounded remaining validity of offline grants. Revocation does not recall delivered bytes or necessarily interrupt an already authorized stream.
T-01/T-02 must choose and encode candidate-result handoff semantics. Either retain a bounded recoverable result (or immutable reference) until durable acknowledgement/acceptance permits disposal, or explicitly allow loss and apply finite replay/reauthorization policy only after prior execution is settled. Identify the last recoverable copy and owner at each transfer, including controller death after delivery but before apply, domain rejection, acknowledgement loss and application-commit uncertainty. Processor scratch disposal and candidate-result disposal are different obligations. Apply/retention recovery must reconcile exact acceptance before garbage collection; exceeding retention cannot silently discard an unresolved required copy or create unbounded result storage.
Provide an owned native transaction scope that rechecks current run/attempt/execution authority after locking, then calls application SQL and records application acceptance, native job/attempt completion, events and workflow consequences in the same transaction. There is no acknowledged application commit followed by a separate success write. Expose reusable in-transaction native transitions through the existing owned SQLx foundation; do not call the current independently committing public success entrypoint from the callback or add a parallel transaction abstraction. Current domain authority is application-owned and checked in that same transaction. Duplicate applications must be idempotent or rejected; lost commit acknowledgement is reconciled from that exact invocation/acceptance identity before replay. The runtime must not repeat application SQL after reconciling an identified committed acceptance; the callback can run again after a confirmed rolled-back attempt under explicit retry policy. No owned connection/transaction or separately paired commit token is supplied on the canonical path. PgScopedSql exposes a query executor for trusted SQL; it cannot prevent explicit transaction-control SQL, direct manipulation of ledger tables, or effects through independently captured clients. Those are excluded escapes, not supported compositions or evidence of rollback when detected. T-02 must record this upstream/application trust boundary under ADR-010, demonstrate the explicit-COMMIT negative control, and name any minimal shared SQLx seam needed; do not build a SQL sandbox or weaken ordinary library-owned completion. Runledger performs no non-database execution/transport I/O while holding the application transaction. Arbitrary async callbacks can perform external I/O; those effects remain application-owned and outside the atomicity guarantee. Isolation and result authentication do not establish application-level result correctness, malware absence or arbitrary remote rollback.
Diagnostics use bounded codes and redacted reports; raw input/output/stderr are not automatic logs or durable results.

D-07 — Accepted: evidence-led deployment selection without a mandatory provider or remote service.
T-01 compares (a) an existing trusted Runledger worker next to established local isolation, with the producer elsewhere, (b) an optional binding to an established managed execution service, and (c) a narrow authenticated remote runner where trust/deployment requirements justify it. Provider-specific SDKs may live in optional adapters; the core and application contract remain provider-independent. Moving a worker changes which host holds application/database authority; document that tradeoff rather than treating it as equivalent to a credential-isolated remote broker.
Select two materially different supported deployment models and only the bindings they require. They may share an isolation primitive or adapter; two identical hosts or an RPC wrapper around a local handle do not establish diversity. T-05 implements the selected first binding; T-06 proves the second model and implements another binding/remote protocol only if needed. T-01 updates their concrete scope and reuse edge before downstream execution. A custom runner is limited to bounded start/observe/stop/recover and inventory; no business queue, workflow/retry policy, host placement or fleet lifecycle.
For each candidate, map controller/worker, broker if any, processor, ledger/inventory and sensitive artifact placement, privileges/credentials, enforcement owner and recovery operator. Separately state application portability, executor deployability and operational prerequisites. The evaluation must address a restricted managed-container deployment model without privileged orchestration in the application container, and disclose any independently operated privileged service elsewhere. T-01 names the actual target deployment test required before claiming that operational problem solved; T-08 records its evidence. Local restriction emulation can support only the exercised claims, not substitute for a hosted result. Cloud provisioning needs separate authorization; missing access leaves that target unverified, not falsely complete.
Generic runtime APIs contain no Docker/Kubernetes/cloud resource specification. Native SQLx/PostgreSQL 18 remains authoritative. A warm trusted broker may be reused with fresh processor containment. Additional profiles, warm native-processor reuse, a new weaker supervised mode, extra backend families, generic artifact frameworks and nonessential operator UI are deferred. No universal shell runner, plugin marketplace, antivirus service, application policy engine or arbitrary user-code hosting platform.

## Primary references
Checked during architecture review on 2026-09-26; recheck exact selected upstream releases in T-01 and record them in docs/references.md during implementation.
- TLS 1.3: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-1 — confidentiality, integrity and peer authentication are separate transport requirements.
- Docker security: https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/ — daemon authority and runtime isolation depend on configuration.
- Kubernetes Pods: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/ — containers in one Pod share networking; grouping alone is not the declared boundary.
- Kubernetes Jobs: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/job/#handling-pod-and-container-failures — parallelism=1 and restartPolicy=Never can still produce duplicate starts; physical execution and replacement semantics need verification. Rechecked 2026-09-26.
- Managed timeout example: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/job_timeouts.html — best-effort timeout termination and per-attempt countdowns are not an independently proven total lifetime bound. Rechecked 2026-09-26.
- Kubernetes RuntimeClass: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/runtime-class/ — backend selection is a deployment mechanism.
- AWS Fargate security: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-security-considerations.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html — task boundaries and unsupported Docker-style controls illustrate why profiles cannot be flag translations.
- Wasmtime security/interruption: https://docs.wasmtime.dev/security.html and https://docs.wasmtime.dev/examples-interrupting-wasm.html — optional capability-based mechanisms; no native-workload compatibility claim.

## Alternatives
Ordinary subprocess + env_clear supplies useful supervision, not the protected isolation boundary. A mandatory container-per-job/cloud-task application API fixes one deployment shape. A provider-neutral trait that leaves lifecycle coordination to applications retains the original problem. Optional bindings to established platforms are live T-01 alternatives under D-07. Building a new sandbox or general orchestration service exceeds this epic.

No second queue, invented sandbox or unverified portability/security claim is introduced. Required target deployment evidence remains an incomplete acceptance item until executed; optional/unavailable environments are explicitly excluded from support claims.

fields.title: T-01: Prove a deployable isolation approach and its operational recovery
fields.description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-01. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Select the first protected profile and simplest feasible execution approach, with reproducible containment/recovery evidence and two materially different deployment models under D-07.

## Context
Resolve D-02/D-04/D-07 before production APIs depend on runtime assumptions. Existing Runledger subprocess ownership does not supply these guarantees.

## Changes
First specify one profile assuming a fully compromised registered workload: protected assets, allowed input/result/filesystem/egress, resource/time limits, plaintext/scratch/result handling and supported enforcement-failure domains. Use one representative registered native workload plus a hostile fixture; keep names/scenarios generic. Inspect versions/licenses, input immutability, native dependencies, subprocesses and scratch requirements. Compare the three D-07 topology families on paper; prove at most two shortlisted mechanisms, not an open-ended runtime survey.
Deliver a deployment/privilege/credential map, explicit operational-cost comparison, observed capability matrix, time/skew/enforcement contract, physical execution identity and backend retry/replacement rules, candidate-result ownership/retention-or-recompute decision, and recovery inventory owner. Separate application portability from executor and operator prerequisites. Identify Linux/macOS controller support and unsupported local profiles; name the actual restricted-hosting target and its required acceptance test without introducing a mandatory cloud dependency.
Rehearse ambiguous execution at full reserved capacity in the bounded spike inventory: who contains/reconciles which infrastructure identity, what permits reuse, what remains quarantined, and what reserved control resources keep recovery possible. Select and record the two deployment models in D-07 and revise T-05/T-06 titles/surfaces and any binding-reuse dependency before downstream work. Keep experiment code separate until adopted; no production abstraction is approved by an unexecuted design. Full native ledger integration belongs to T-03/T-04; this spike must not implement a parallel production queue.

## Recovery
Use disposable synthetic inputs and bounded disposable resources. Stop/fence discovered invocations and retain unresolved evidence; do not broaden host privileges or weaken the profile to make the spike pass. An unsupported requirement becomes a concrete design decision before dependent tasks begin.

## Verification policy
Follow the epic verification and rollout contract and the applicable repository/package guides. Record actual commands, revisions, platform/backend prerequisites and outcomes here. Runtime/security/platform claims require executable evidence; this planned task is unexecuted. New public APIs require rustdoc, examples and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
Verification: Run the representative processor within the chosen restrictions and independently observe hostile filesystem, network/metadata, credential, descendant and resource/output denial. Kill or stop the controller and broker separately while the processor environment remains alive; partition communication, delay start until after stop, and exercise restart/reboot/clock uncertainty within the declared fault model. A broker timer alone is not independent enforcement. Test backend-initiated replacement without a new dispatch and show it cannot start an unaccounted or overlapping processor under the initial profile. Exercise controller death after candidate delivery but before apply using the chosen recovery policy. Fill outstanding capacity, lose observability and demonstrate verified settlement/containment or an explicit actionable unavailable state.

Done when: The first profile and supported failure assumptions are fixed; the simplest feasible topology is selected from the compared alternatives, with exact reproducible evidence and accepted operator prerequisites/cost. Two materially different deployment models and their actual acceptance tests are named. Required hard bounds are either demonstrated under the declared faults or the candidate is rejected. T-05/T-06 scope and actual dependency edges match the decision; a custom remote service is not mandatory. Missing hosted access leaves the affected proof/claim unverified and cannot be replaced by local-only evidence. If no candidate satisfies the required profile, leave the task open with the concrete unsupported requirement.

fields.title: T-02: Define protected processor contracts and an adversarial executor test harness
fields.description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-02. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Expose a small native contract that binds processors to validated isolation requirements and represents execution evidence without conflating results, termination or cleanup.

## Context
D-01 through D-06 and ADR-010. Use T-01's proven semantics; names are implementation choices, while invalid-state prevention is required.

## Changes
Extend runledger-core job/handler contracts and the minimal runledger-runtime catalog seam; identify optional adapter package boundaries. Add only the opaque processor/profile/invocation values, bounded input/output descriptors, redacted exhaustive outcomes and typed observations required by the selected protected path. Keep internal phases inside library-owned execution; do not expose a type per phase to consumers or add a new supervised mode. Define protocol identity/version/expiry and authorized input/result transfer. Build a reusable conformance harness with controllable launch/stop/transport faults and hostile native fixtures; keep owning-suite fixtures out of generic leaf test-support. Define stable invocation lineage across native replay/workflow recovery, distinct from each physical execution identity. Carry T-01 time-source, enforcement-owner, skew and reboot/expiry decisions in the contract. Encode physical execution multiplicity/internal replacement, aggregate accounting and the selected result-handoff acknowledgements, last-copy ownership, retention and loss/recompute policy before T-03 fixes persistence. Distinguish scratch settlement from result disposal.
Use a small compiling generic consumer to exercise preparation, authorization and application before either deployment implementation hardens the API. Close the D-06 SQL capability decision: ordinary transaction ownership/completion stays in the library, while arbitrary transaction-control/direct-ledger SQL and captured external clients are excluded trust-boundary escapes. Inspect PgScopedSql and existing in-transaction native transitions; identify any minimal shared batter-sqlx seam and record the ADR-010 reason local types cannot prove arbitrary SQL/external effects. Do not introduce a SQL sandbox. Confirm T-01 has finalized T-05/T-06 surfaces and reuse edges before closing this task.

## Recovery
Keep new APIs opt-in and old handlers unchanged. Revise a contract that cannot express T-01's actual semantics before persistence/adapters adopt it; do not retain a misleading safe alias for a weaker path.

## Verification policy
Follow the epic verification and rollout contract and the applicable repository/package guides. Record actual commands, revisions, platform/backend prerequisites and outcomes here. Runtime/security/platform claims require executable evidence; this planned task is unexecuted. New public APIs require rustdoc, examples and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
Verification: Compile-fail checks reject unsupported ordinary compositions, forged application settlement, pairing the wrong identity and silent supervised-process substitution. Construction rejects inconsistent resource/time limits before execution. Harness assertions distinguish result receipt from stop/cleanup and include negative controls that a lying/late fake adapter fails. Check framing/length/protocol-version handling and redaction. No fake execution counts as isolation evidence. Include substrate-initiated duplicate/replacement and result-delivered/controller-dead-before-apply negative controls. Exercise explicit COMMIT as a documented excluded escape: detection must not be reported as undoing committed effects. Compile-fail checks cover extractable connection/transaction ownership and paired completion tokens, not a false claim to reject arbitrary SQL text.

Done when: The contract and harness can drive the selected deployment models without mandatory provider identifiers or raw launch/kill obligations in a consumer. The proactive invalid-state review records every remaining application/upstream assumption; the early consumer and rustdoc compile, result ownership and physical multiplicity are explicit, and the SQL boundary decision is closed before persistence/runtime implementation.

fields.title: T-03: Persist invocation ownership and capacity beyond job lease expiry
fields.description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-03. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Durable identity, recovery fencing and execution capacity survive lost responses, lease expiry, cancellation, dead-lettering and process death.

## Context
D-04/D-05. Existing job_execution_resource_claims are lease-scoped; protected invocation resources need independent settlement without altering ordinary jobs.

## Changes
Add forward-only native migrations in runledger/migrations and mirrored packages; extend runledger-postgres jobs/queue claim, lifecycle, reaper, recovery and retention paths. Atomically reserve bounded capacity and record immutable invocation identity before launch; retain processor/profile/backend revision, durable expiry, observed facts, stop intent and tombstones. Persist the T-02 physical execution mapping and separate compute/scratch/candidate-result obligations, including result acknowledgement/acceptance and disposal eligibility or explicit result-loss classification. Add concurrency-safe recovery ownership with takeover fencing and monotonic terminal observations. Gate replacement launches, result application and purge. Define version/capability activation guards for all writers including old reapers/admin operations; synchronize SQLx metadata. Specify one deterministic lock order and the post-lock authority/expiry linearization point shared by result application, completion and recovery; expose reusable in-transaction native transition internals for T-04 under T-02's trusted-SQL contract; do not compose a second independently committed success transaction. Cover jobs/admin replay and jobs/workflows/{recovery,active_claims} explicitly: preserve/check source invocation lineage across fresh job IDs and gate active-key/resource release on unresolved processor work.

## Recovery
Keep dispatch disabled through migration and retain applied schemas and unresolved rows. Roll forward database defects; stop new admission while compatible recovery continues. Never repair capacity by deleting an unknown invocation or cascading it with a job row.

## Verification policy
Follow the epic verification and rollout contract and the applicable repository/package guides. Record actual commands, revisions, platform/backend prerequisites and outcomes here. Runtime/security/platform claims require executable evidence; this planned task is unexecuted. New public APIs require rustdoc, examples and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
Verification: PostgreSQL 18 multi-connection tests cover last-slot races, stale recovery owners, expired job lease with live invocation, cancel/reap/replay/dead-letter transitions, same-identity conflicts, lost commit acknowledgement, restart expiry, delayed launch, reported physical replacement state, last-copy result acknowledgement/disposal, job deletion/retention and tombstone expiry. Database tests establish ledger invariants; real substrate enforcement remains T-05/T-06/T-08 evidence. Inspect independent durable state and actual claim behavior. Demonstrate ordinary job/resource behavior is unchanged and incompatible writers, including an old transaction resumed after activation, cannot bypass the selected exclusion protocol. Recovery resources remain available when processor capacity is saturated. With capacity greater than one, cancel a workflow processor, expire its lease while the execution survives, recover/clone the workflow, including recovery-of-recovery and concurrent recovery requests, into fresh job IDs and prove replacement dispatch remains blocked until verified settlement. Check direct replay and active-key reenqueue too; distinguish unrelated new roots under application-owned exclusion policy.

Done when: All processor launch/replay/application paths consult the durable invocation gate; unresolved execution remains accounted across replicas and terminal jobs. Recovery is bounded and can make progress independently of a handler lease. Migration/retention and mixed-writer rules are executable, and commit ambiguity is retained.

fields.title: T-04: Drive processor jobs and apply results under current execution authority
fields.description:
Canonical plan: br show batter-05ci --json (epic description and design).
Task: T-04. Delivery scope and acceptance live in this Bead; native blocker edges own ordering.

## Outcome
Canonical processor registration owns every execution phase, and stale results cannot cause application SQL or successful job completion.

## Context
D-03/D-04/D-06. Reuse JobExecution and native settlement; consumer callbacks own domain authorization and result meaning, not launch/cleanup mechanics.

## Changes
Extend native runtime catalog/worker execution/completion, settlement and recovery driving. Own capacity acquisition, intent registration, fresh authorization before input release, dispatch, deadline/lease-loss stop, result validation, the selected recoverable-result handoff or bounded loss/recompute outcome, and separate execution/scratch/result settlement independent of waiters. Supply a native owned SQL transaction scope that checks current job/run/attempt/invocation authority after locks and commits the callback's SQL, application acceptance, native job/attempt completion, events and workflow consequences atomically using the existing owned SQLx foundation and reusable in-transaction native transitions under T-02's explicitly trusted-SQL boundary. Expose no independently owned transaction or paired commit token. Preserve concrete errors, commit uncertainty, dispatch through destruction and opt-in legacy compatibility. Distinguish local settled dependencies from remotely unresolved durable handoff. The canonical runtime consumes an opaque finalized observation instead of performing the legacy success write a second time.

## Recovery

## Outcome
An application can execute registered native workloads on untrusted inputs through one Runledger-owned invocation path without implementing launch, timeout, cancellation, join, cleanup or retry coordination. Feasibility evidence selects the execution approach; a local-plus-custom-remote adapter pair is not predetermined. The same protected application contract must work in two materially different deployment models under explicit, verified prerequisites. No provider-specific topology is imposed on the application API.

## Scope and authority
This epic is the canonical cross-task decision record. Child Beads own delivery scope, acceptance, priority, status and native blocker edges. Stable T-01 through T-08 identifiers are retained in task titles and external references; there is no parallel Markdown backlog.

The requested work is planning. Implementation tasks remain open and unclaimed. Implementation includes native Runledger contracts/persistence/runtime, only the execution bindings required by the selected deployment models, a generic consumer and conformance evidence. The draft-PR workflow is authorized. Infrastructure provisioning, hosted deployment and publication require their own authorization; this planning epic does not authorize them. Do not modify the motivating application's active migration as part of this epic.

Ordinary handlers keep their existing supported contracts. The new protected processor path must not silently select a weaker backend. Unix-only scope remains; Linux and macOS controllers stay in scope, with unsupported local isolation capabilities explicitly rejected and remote execution available where verified.

## Evidence
Fact: source inspected at 74238a2dffe29aee681440c566d6bcb42e742e30. runledger/runledger-core/src/jobs/{handler,execution,status}.rs provide trusted handlers, live deadlines/progress and retry kinds. runledger/runledger-runtime/src/worker/execution.rs stops polling a handler after deadline or lease loss; it does not establish external-process termination.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Durable execution resources, and runledger/migrations/202607280004_job_execution_resources.up.sql define lease-scoped single-permit reservations released through job transitions/reaping. These cannot bound executions that survive their job lease.
Fact: native settlement lives in runledger/runledger-runtime/src/{settlement,task_group,supervisor}/. runledger/runledger-postgres/src/jobs/queue/{claim,reaper,lifecycle}.rs and associated directories own queue transitions; reuse them rather than adding a second queue.
Fact: an inspected upload-processing consumer's repair history repeatedly addressed disposable-container cleanup, parser/host failure attribution and bounded retries. Its unfinished migration replaced container launch with environment-cleared subprocesses. Source inspection is not executed isolation evidence; no defect-rate or final-consumer claim is made. This anonymized rationale is sufficient; another private checkout is not an implementation prerequisite.
Fact: crates/batter-sqlx/src/atomic/scope.rs exposes PgScopedSql::executor and explicitly permits SQL with irreversible effects such as COMMIT; boundary-loss detection is not rollback. The inspected regression source crates/batter-sqlx/tests/atomic_live/fail_fast_loss.rs exercises committed writes despite scope loss. runledger-postgres/src/atomic.rs reuses that capability, while jobs/queue/lifecycle/success.rs currently owns its own transaction. These sources were inspected, not executed, during this amendment.
Fact: runledger/README.md, Quick start, supports separate producer and worker processes sharing PostgreSQL. Hosting an existing trusted worker beside a proven local executor is a candidate deployment, not proof of processor isolation.
Inference: reusable execution ownership and isolation-binding contracts can remove this repeated application protocol, but backend support, operator burden and deployment assumptions must be demonstrated.
Existing related work: batter-44w, batter-gg8 and batter-0cp are completed foundations, not proof of this capability. batter-7g0 concerns diagnostic correlation and must not become an authority prerequisite.

## Verification and completion
All eight delivery tasks must meet their acceptance. The same representative registered native workload and hostile fixture corpus must execute through the two selected deployment models. A fake adapter, loopback transport or a second identical host alone is insufficient isolation or deployment-diversity evidence. Cover controller/runner death, delayed launch after cancellation, lease takeover, result/commit uncertainty, descendant escape attempts, resource/output exhaustion, credential/filesystem/network denial, current-authority rejection and upgrade/retention compatibility. Include fresh-agent implementation and modification exercises; label them proposed/unexecuted until recorded.

Use focused checks during each task and the repository's applicable complete backend verification before delivery. Record exact revisions, operating systems, backend versions, commands, prerequisites and results in the owning Bead. Update rustdoc/examples, relevant contracts, implemented-status rows, docs/references.md and verification input ownership when implementation lands. Do not present this planning session as runtime, Linux/macOS or hosted-CI verification.

## Rollout and recovery
Use additive migrations and versioned invocation/protocol/profile identifiers. Keep processor dispatch disabled until database guards and every active worker/reaper/admin writer that could claim, reap, replay, cancel or purge processor jobs are compatible or fenced out. Job-type filtering alone does not protect old reapers. Prefer a coordinated cutover when it meets deployment needs; mixed-version operation is not a goal by itself. Preserve legacy job semantics and test actual old/new binaries, including an old session/transaction resumed across activation, against the selected writer-exclusion policy.
Start with synthetic inputs. Stop new processor admission on containment; durably record stop intent, revoke further input access, reconcile outstanding invocations and retain their capacity/tombstones. Plaintext already delivered cannot be recalled. A failed job or expired lease does not prove stopped execution. Never clear an unresolved execution as a normal retry or delete applied schema/history for rollback. Disabling admission must leave a compatible recovery owner running.
Normal bounded shutdown may hand remote recovery to a durable owner only after acknowledged persistence and settlement of local users of dependencies. Report that handoff separately from remote termination; it is not a clean external-execution result.

## Risks and open decisions
T-01 owns the first protected profile, representative processor, deployment selection, failure assumptions, physical execution multiplicity, result-handoff strategy and operational cost. Compare separate native workers with local isolation, an existing managed executor, and a narrow remote runner on equal footing. Limit the comparison to those three topology families and actual mechanism proofs to at most two shortlisted choices; use one representative registered native workload plus hostile fixtures. A new remote service is justified only by a demonstrated trust/deployment need.
T-01 closure must record the chosen models, exact privileges/services/inventories and operating owner, an actionable uncertainty-recovery exercise, and the deployment tests required to establish the intended supported environments. It must revise D-07 and T-05/T-06 scope/edges to its findings before T-02 closes. It can choose a simpler topology without weakening the protected contract or removing deployment-diversity evidence. If no candidate meets the selected required profile, retain the blocker; do not invent a sandbox or silently weaken a guarantee.
T-02 closes only after the SQL capability boundary, result-copy ownership/acknowledgements, backend retry/multiplicity rules and a small compiling consumer are explicit. T-03 owns locking, reservations and writer activation. T-08 rehearses an already designed recovery procedure and records final deployment evidence. Application authorization, application-level result correctness, application content policy, external publication and forensic erasure remain outside library guarantees.
Strict no-overlap and workflow-lineage coverage remain the initial supported policy, with their availability cost recorded in D-05; they are not logical consequences of handling untrusted inputs. Accounted overlapping transformations or a direct-jobs-only scope are alternatives requiring an explicit contract/scope amendment, not implementation shortcuts.
The first safe delivery action is T-01; later implementation is conditional on its closure decisions. After T-02, persistence and the first execution binding can proceed independently when shared interfaces settle. Runtime follows persistence. The second deployment task depends on the first binding only if selected reuse requires it; record that edge before either dependent task starts. Consumer integration and final acceptance follow both deployment proofs.

## Planning validation
The original critical-profile structural check passed with eight tasks, no errors and no warnings. Earlier focused reviews repaired encrypted transport, distributed expiry, atomic application/native completion and workflow-lineage omissions. Two subsequent user-supplied reviews prompted this amendment: correct the trusted SQL boundary, make deployment selection evidence-led, expose executor multiplicity and result-handoff decisions, and bring operational recovery proof forward. Prior review closure is historical, not a claim that later findings were impossible.
The user authorized T-01 to replace the prescribed adapter pair when a simpler deployment approach preserves security and portability.
